chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Ali from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from Isma'il al-Ju'fi who said:
I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'The grandfather shares equally with the brothers, regardless of how many there are, even if they are one hundred thousand.'

key_terms.الْجَدُّ: The grandfather (paternal ancestor) in inheritance law
key_terms.مَا بَلَغُوا: As many as they are / regardless of quantity

ai.seo_question: How does the grandfather inherit in relation to the brothers in Shia Islamic law?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the status of the paternal grandfather (al-jadd) as a primary heir who shares equally with the brothers (or grandfathers with grandfathers), a ruling that underscores the principle of 'equal shares for equal degrees' regardless of the number of co-heirs. In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith is pivotal in resolving the debate between the 'hajb' (exclusion) and 'qasama' (division) schools, affirming that the grandfather does not exclude brothers but rather shares the estate with them. This establishes the grandfather's position as a 'root' heir (asl) rather than a 'branch' heir (far'), ensuring his right to inheritance is robust and not diminished by numerous siblings.
